payload.title: What Are the Turkish Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s, often with a Turkish partner, parent or grandparent, who are planning or attending a wedding with Turkish roots (in Türkiye or elsewhere) and want to know what each custom means, what happens in what order from the asking to the last halay, and what marrying legally in Türkiye involves for Australians.
payload.goal: Read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine (primary CTA); secondary, in-context invitation to speak with a Wedded Advisor placed straight after the legal section on marrying in Türkiye.
payload.service_link: /magazine (primary, UTM-tagged); /wonderland-concierge (secondary, UTM-tagged, after the legal section)
payload.angle: Page-one listicles (and our own old page) jumble the asking, the henna night, the procession and the reception, state folklore like salted coffee and foot-stepping as fact, and skip the law. We follow a Turkish wedding in order (kız isteme, söz and nişan, çeyiz, kına gecesi, the day, the takı and the halay), explain who does what, separate sourced meaning from what is only 'often told', note that customs vary by region and family, and add what Australians need and listicles skip: that the civil marriage at the municipal marriage office is the legal one, the documents Australians are asked for from official sources only, and Smartraveller's current Türkiye levels as at November 2026. It is the Turkish chapter of our sourced wedding traditions pillar.
must_include: Exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways at the top.

10 to 12 customs from tradition_plan in wedding order, grouped before the day and the day itself, each with a sourced meaning; unsourced origins labelled 'often told' or left out. Turkish spelling with diacritics in copy (kız isteme, söz, nişan, çeyiz, kına gecesi, bindallı, takı töreni, davul and zurna, halay); Türkiye for the country.
A line that customs vary by region, family and faith (urban and rural, Anatolian regions), with specific variation only where sourced.

A legal section for Australians marrying in Türkiye: the civil marriage at the municipal marriage office (evlendirme dairesi) is the legally valid one; documents from the Australian Embassy Ankara or Consulate-General Istanbul and Turkish government pages only; 'a fee applies' only if an official source says so, otherwise 'check with the marriage office and the embassy, including any fees'; 'as at November 2026'.

Smartraveller's overall level (Exercise a high degree of caution) with the page date (updated 30 October 2026), the higher-level areas named (Do not travel within 10km of the Syrian border; Reconsider your need to travel to Hakkari and Şırnak provinces), a note that Türkiye does not legally recognise same-sex marriage (Smartraveller), and a prompt to check Smartraveller before booking; any destination suggestion sits outside those areas.
Internal link to the pillar /expert-advice/wedding-traditions in the intro and the close, and /destinations/europe/turkey from the legal or destination paragraph.
Short FAQ (5 to 6 questions) from SEO People Also Ask, sourced answers only; primary CTA /magazine, secondary Wedded Advisor CTA after the legal section; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md.

tradition_plan.note: Planner fact-checks in 2 parallel batches with separate scratch folders, 15 min hard, save after every 3 facts, no extra sourcing rounds. Preferred sources: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (ich.unesco.org), Türkiye's Ministry of Culture and Tourism (ktb.gov.tr, goturkiye.com), Turkish museums, Britannica, academic or university sources (e.g. DergiPark journal articles). Legal: Smartraveller, Australian Embassy Ankara (turkey.embassy.gov.au) and Consulate-General Istanbul, Turkish government pages (e-Devlet, municipal evlendirme pages, Ministry of Interior). Not found in time: 'often told' or drop.

batch_B.tradition: Legal section: Australians marrying in Türkiye
facts_to_source: Civil marriage at the municipal marriage office (evlendirme dairesi) is the legally recognised form; religious ceremony alone is not (official source)
